content:
Sigmant is described on its own page as an automated crypto trading platform. The page says it offers a 97% prediction accuracy and gives a $250 minimum deposit, with demo funds and round-the-clock support. The page reports strong early interest and support at all hours.

The sections below examine the page's points on sign-up, deposits, tools, fees and help, and the things to confirm first. The page omits the regulator, the licence number and the operator, which left us unable to confirm them. Each claim comes from the platform, except where we indicate otherwise.

Sigmant Explained: What the Platform Describes

Sigmant presents itself as automated crypto trading platform. Its selling points are automated tools, a demo account and support, and the operator is not described.

Sigmant: Where It Delivers, Where It Doesn’t

Sigmant strengths, per its description:

  • The page states a $250 minimum deposit and lists several funding methods, including paypal.
  • A practice account with simulated funds is offered, so the tools can be tried before any real money is used.
  • Support around the clock is advertised, a useful feature if you run into a payment problem.
  • The page makes a specific claim about results (a 97% prediction accuracy), which is at least easy to check against your own demo results.

Where Sigmant Falls Short:

  • No regulator, licence number or operating company is named, so its regulatory status cannot be checked from the page.
  • The a 97% prediction accuracy figure has no period, method or source. The page cites blockchain communities and feedback platforms without naming them.
  • The page mentions reputable brokers without naming any of them.
  • The page leaves out how long withdrawals take and what fees apply.
  • The page rules out Cyprus, Israel and Iran but leaves the position of other countries unexplained.

What Actually Happens Behind Sigmant

The page says an automated system analyses market data and places trades for you, with the option to set your own strategies. The page presents its tools as straightforward.

The page leaves out the signal method, the data sources and how accuracy was calculated. Before trusting a signal, obtain written responses to these questions.

Getting Set Up: What the Process Looks Like

1. Register

Enter your first name, last name, email address, phone number and place of residence, then confirm the email you receive.

2. Deposit

The minimum deposit is $250. PayPal, Skrill, debit or credit cards and direct transfers from a bank are the listed payment options. Look into the currency and any bank fees ahead of payment.

3. Practise first

Use the demo account with simulated funds before you fund a live account. Test a withdrawal with a small amount.

Breaking Down What Sigmant Costs

The page says there are no deposit or withdrawal charges and no undisclosed fees. The page lacks a fee schedule, leaving trading spreads, commissions and currency fees uncertain.

  • Minimum deposit: $250.
  • Registration fee: none listed.
  • Deposit and withdrawal fees are said to be nil, with no schedule to support it.
  • Trading spreads and commissions: not itemised.
Learn More

Which Assets Sigmant Covers

The page describes a crypto trading system and refers to digital coins, but it does not list the individual assets it trades.

  • Cryptocurrencies, as described on the page
  • No individual assets listed
  • Available except in Cyprus, Israel and Iran, per the page
Discover More

Is Sigmant Legit?

Safety measures are described, along with user responses and expert views, yet no regulator, licence or company is identified. We were unable to establish its regulation from what we examined.

  • The operating company should be found on the regulator's official register before any deposit. The page does not name it.
  • The a 97% prediction accuracy figure and the user responses have no named source.
  • The platform calls itself 'fact-checked' and 'authentic', a self-description the page does not allow us to test.
Learn More

Mistakes Worth Avoiding on Sigmant

Most losses with automated or analyst-led platforms come from user decisions rather than the platform itself. A few worth flagging:

Trusting the accuracy figure

An a 97% prediction accuracy figure with no method cannot be checked. Treat it as a marketing claim.

Depositing a large sum at once

Start with the $250 minimum and test a withdrawal before adding more.

Skipping the regulator check

No regulator is named, so confirm the company yourself before you register.

Overlooking the country rules

The page excludes three countries. Make sure the service is legal for residents of your area.

Learn More

A Quick Checklist Before Your First Live Trade

Run through this before committing real funds.

  • The official register should list the operating company and its regulator.
  • Written confirmation of the $250 minimum and payment routes is needed.
  • Written confirmation of how long withdrawals take and what they cost is needed.
  • A small withdrawal tested before depositing more.
  • The a 97% prediction accuracy figure read as a claim, not a forecast.
  • Open the platform by keying in its web address.
Explore Sigmant

Who Gets the Most Out of Sigmant

Sigmant may suit a beginner who wants a guided, automated tool, starts with the $250 minimum and accepts that the money could be lost. The service is not well matched to people who require a named regulator, published fees or reliable results.

Base your view on checkable facts rather than homepage assurances.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Sigmant legit?

We could not confirm it. Because the page names no regulator, licence or operator, search the regulator's register before you deposit.

Is Sigmant a scam?

We cannot say either way. The page's claims are beyond our checks, so trial a small withdrawal and register only through the address you typed.

What is the Sigmant minimum deposit?

$250, according to the page.

Does Sigmant charge fees?

Deposits and withdrawals are said to be free, although the page supplies no fee schedule.

Does Sigmant have a demo account?

A demo account using simulated money is described on the page.

Is Sigmant available in my country?

According to the page, Cyprus, Israel and Iran are excluded. Check the sign-up form for your country.

Does Sigmant guarantee profits?

No. The a 97% prediction accuracy figure is a claim on the page, and no profit is guaranteed.

Where We Land on Sigmant

Sigmant presents an automated crypto trading tool with a $250 minimum deposit, a demo account and round-the-clock support, according to its own page. No source supports the headline accuracy figure, and the page names no regulator or operator.

If you still plan to use it, confirm the company with the regulator, get written fee and withdrawal terms and run a withdrawal test first.
